problem: All VLN methods assume a single agent navigating in isolation with egocentric observations and can only accumulate knowledge from places it has itself visited; no work studies whether observations from other concurrently navigating agents (each with its own instruction and goal) help.
motivation: In real settings, multiple robots often share the same space, and partial observability bottlenecks long-horizon VLN. Peer observations could expand an agent's perceptual coverage without extra exploration (35% to 65% coverage in the paper's motivating figure).
key_idea: Co-VLN: independently navigating agents detect spatial overlap between their topological graphs and merge them via anchor nodes, so each agent plans over an enriched graph including peers' explored regions.
insight: Sharing peers' topological memory consistently helps both a learned model (DUET) and a zero-shot MLLM agent (MapGPT), and gains grow with scene size (SR +1.98 small, +3.41 medium, +4.56 large) and with overlap (prior-based pairing beats random pairing). The fusion ablation shows early, bidirectional and persistent merging is best (SR 74.5/SPL 62.3, versus 72.4/60.0 without persistence). Peer count saturates around 4 agents.
method: Independent navigation: each agent runs an unmodified baseline (DUET, MapGPT, ETPNav) and builds its own topological graph G_t^i (nodes are viewpoints storing embeddings, images or text).

Spatial overlap detection (DUET): a lightweight Transformer discriminator f_theta on node-embedding pairs gives confidence c; a match is declared when c exceeds a threshold tau, and c is converted to a distance d=(1-c)*alpha.
Spatial overlap detection (MapGPT / R2R-CE): ID-based matching of simulator viewpoint IDs (oracle), or GPS distance <0.5 m in R2R-CE.

Collaborative knowledge fusion: augment agent i's graph with the unmatched nodes and edges of agent j plus bridge edges at anchor nodes (distance-weighted for embeddings, zero-distance merge for IDs). This is symmetric, and the agent then keeps its original policy on the fused graph.

Task construction: R2R episodes are grouped into pairs (N=2) within the same scan; prior-based pairing greedily maximizes ground-truth path overlap (4.24 overlapping viewpoints per pair vs 0.88 for random); 5 unpaired episodes become self-pairs.
MapGPT prompt modification: adds a Supplementary_Map field and other_* peer images/places to the prompt. DUET and ETPNav are fine-tuned under the sharing setting (DUET 20k iterations, ETPNav 8k).

numbers_note: Baselines are re-run by the authors: DUET 71.52/60.41, DUET+ScaleVLN 79.40/69.97, MapGPT-Qwen3-VL-32B 52.19/44.73, ETPNav 57.21/49.15. The peer-scaling and MLLM ablations use only the R2R-Hard Subset. The paper does not state whether the MapGPT DUET† ID-based rows and the embedding-based row share the same test conditions beyond what is noted.
results: Vision-sharing raises DUET from SR 71.52/SPL 60.41 to 74.54/62.28 (76.23/62.90 with oracle IDs). Adding it to DUET+ScaleVLN gives SR 82.46/SPL 73.39, the best on R2R val-unseen. Zero-shot MapGPT (Qwen3-VL-32B) improves from 52.19 to 55.81 SR, above SpatialGPT (48.4) and MSNav (46.0). ETPNav on R2R-CE gains +1.95 SR and +2.64 SPL.
limitations: Evaluation relies on constructed concurrent episodes, with prior-based pairing using GT path overlap; random pairing yields much smaller gains (e.g. MapGPT SR 53.4 vs 55.8), and real deployments lack such prior knowledge.

Idealized assumptions: perfect instant graph exchange, no communication cost or latency, and oracle viewpoint IDs (MapGPT rows use IDs, DUET† uses oracle); embedding-based detection is imperfect (74.54 vs 76.23 SR).

Only R2R and R2R-CE with two-agent pairs, pairs run in parallel with no real-time asynchrony modeled; scaling and MLLM analyses are on a 200-episode subset from one scan; gains saturate beyond about 4 peers.
